faults.finding: 'The flux in the iron follows the volts per hertz' is stated, not explained. Why a lower frequency at the same voltage gives more flux is the step the whole lesson rests on.
faults.fix: Add: each half cycle the voltage drives the flux up in the iron; at half the frequency each half cycle lasts twice as long, so full voltage would drive it twice as high.

faults.finding: 'The heavy fan drives the motor faster than its field' skips why: the drive lowers the frequency faster than the fan's inertia lets it slow.
faults.fix: Say the drive drops the frequency fast, the fan cannot slow that quickly, so the rotor runs faster than the field.

faults.finding: 'the motor can still give its rated torque at low speed' read alone in the dossier ignores the self-cooled motor's limit at low speed.
faults.fix: Add one short sentence: its own fan slows too, so a self-cooled motor cannot keep that up continuously.

faults.finding: 'Of the ways to start a motor, it is the only one that also controls speed' is wider than the source, which compares the usual starters; lesson 1 named a wound rotor's resistance speed control.
